file in task state.
FIRST run: ORCH_STATE_DIR="/home/laniakea/Projects/touch/.claude/local-orchestrators/touch-aggregator" bash "/home/laniakea/Projects/touch/.claude/shared/monitoring/status.sh" "synthesis" synthesize running "merging 6 research reports plus driver context"

Research reports (read ALL of them fully from disk first):
- /home/laniakea/Projects/touch/.claude/local-orchestrators/touch-aggregator/findings/research-sessiondata-attempt-1.md — Researched the persisted session data model from real files under ~/.claude plus targeted `grep -a`/`dd` reads of the 275MB CLI binary (v2.1.220), and empirical probes in /tmp. 20 findings, 3 blockers.

WHAT EXISTS. The session JSONL is a mix of four record classes, and the CLI's own classification table (binary byte 259354279) is the ground truth: `transcript` (user/assistant/system/attachment), `boundary-cleared` (progress, file-history-*, last-prompt), `accumulate` (content-replacement, fork-context-ref, frame-link) and `last-wins` (mode, permission-mode, ai-title, custom-title, summary, tag, queue-operation, worktree-state, pr-link, bridge-session, …). Siblings: `<sid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` + `.meta.json`, `<sid>/subagents/workflows/<runId>/journal.jsonl`, `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`, `~/.claude/file-history/<sid>/<hash>@vN`, `~/.claude/history.jsonl`, `~/.claude.json`. There is no `projects/<sid>/workflows/<runId>.json` — that path in the brief does not exist on disk.

THREE BLOCKERS.
1. `usage` is copied onto every split assistant record of one API response — 50 of 63 response groups span multiple records, so summing per record over-counts output tokens 2.09x (115,605 vs 55,396 deduped by `message.id`). `.claude/shared/monitoring/decision_watcher.py:154` already dedupes correctly; reuse it.
2. Thinking text is never persisted: all 44/44 thinking blocks in the main transcript, and every one in all 8 subagent transcripts, have `thinking: ""` with only a signature — despite `alwaysThinkingEnabled: true`. A transcript-sourced "thinking" pane is永 empty.
3. The transcript is not append-only. `performRemoveByUuid` truncates and rewrites the tail (the file shrinks); `performCompactTranscript` rewrites the whole file via `<file>.compact.tmp.<hex>` + rename, dropping everything before the compact boundary. Byte-offset tailing silently freezes.

LATENCY (measured, good news). The writer batches on a `FLUSH_INTERVAL_MS = 100` timer; a poll started inside a Bash call saw that call's own `tool_use` record land +0.10s later, before the tool finished. Intra-turn visibility is real and sub-second with zero instrumentation. The cost is torn tails: batches are one `appendFile` up to 100 MiB, and observed lines reach 46 KB — cut at the last `\n` and defer the remainder.

LIFECYCLE. `/clear` starts a NEW sessionId and new file under the same pid (CLI's own command description), so the sidebar must key on pid and re-resolve sessionId every poll. The transcript file is created lazily — a probe session produced `lastSessionId` in `~/.claude.json` but no `.jsonl` at all. There is no session-end record (a cleanly `/exit`-ed session just stops after `Goodbye!`). `sessions/<pid>.json` is not a heartbeat: it was 863s stale while the session was busy running six subagents, and is written with a non-atomic read-modify-writeFile. Liveness must be `/proc/<pid>` + `procStart` (verified = `/proc/pid/stat` field 22).

AGENT GRAPH. Async `Workflow` runs return only `status: "async_launched"` and never get a completion record in the parent transcript — the run graph exists solely in `journal.jsonl` (which has `started`/`result` entries with **no timestamps**, and a `result` that is a Python-repr string, not JSON). Workflow subagent `.meta.json` is a 63-byte stub with no description or toolUseId, so per-node labels can only come from the `[monitor] plan=… stage=… role=… attempt=…` marker in the agent's first user record.

TERMINAL VIEW VERDICT. Reconstructible: prompts (incl. slash/bash-mode forms), assistant text, every tool call with full input, every tool result with full untruncated output (richer than the TTY, which truncates), turn durations, usage, model/effort/skill attribution, the whole subagent tree, file diffs. Not reconstructible: reasoning, streaming deltas, ANSI, permission dialogs, status line, system prompt, intra-tool progress (`progress` records are in the schema but literally zero exist on disk), and session end. The binary contains a complete asciicast v2 recorder writing `<sid>-<ts>.cast`, but `CLAUDE_CODE_TERMINAL_RECORDING` produced no file in three probes (`-p` with `1`, `-p` with a path, and a real pty) and the literal appears only in env-schema tables — do not plan around it. The plan must explicitly choose: semantic re-render of the transcript, or Touch owns the PTY.

TWO CROSS-CUTTING RISKS. The CLI's retention sweep unlinks the transcript and `rm -rf`s the entire `<sessionId>/` subagent tree, so Touch must own its history rather than reading `~/.claude` as an archive. And transcripts plus `history.jsonl` hold unredacted file contents, command output and every prompt ever typed — with a 0.0.0.0 bind and a published port mandated by the sandbox, every transcript route needs a token.
- /home/laniakea/Projects/touch/.claude/local-orchestrators/touch-aggregator/findings/research-agentgraph-attempt-1.md — Rebuilt the run graph from primary sources (live session dd469822…, workflow wf_829e6f58-b2f, and grep/dd reads of the 2.1.220 CLI binary) and found 17 actionable items, 2 blockers. The harness writes, unconditionally: per-agent transcripts with timestamps and message.usage; sidecars carrying agentType/description/toolUseId/spawnDepth/model (and parentAgentId only for depth-2+); a workflow journal of bare {type,key,agentId[,result]} lines; and, in the parent transcript, the Agent tool_use/tool_result pair and the single Workflow tool_result that names runId/transcriptDir/scriptPath. Everything else a graph wants is either convention or unavailable. Two blockers: (1) the label/phase passed to agent() are never persisted, so every workflow node on disk is an anonymous "workflow-subagent · opus · spawnDepth 1" — node naming is entirely the [monitor] prompt-marker convention; (2) the rich node record (index/label/phaseTitle/state/tokens/toolCalls/durationMs/attempt/resultPreview) lives only in memory and is flushed to <sessionId>/workflows/<runId>.json at exactly one call site, in the completion path, so it cannot drive a live graph. Majors: journal lines have no timestamps and journal order is not spawn order (proved — append order differs from transcript-first-timestamp order for the 6 parallel researchers); a 180s stall watchdog with up to 5 retries makes one logical node emit multiple "started" entries with new agentIds, which decision_watcher's stale-close guard provably never closes (phantom forever-running nodes); the journal key is a content hash so identical prompts collide and resumed runs replay agents with no journal entry at all; queued agents have zero disk footprint and the concurrency cap is min(16,max(2,cpus-2)), so the same fan-out renders smaller on a small host; transcript and snapshot paths key off the CURRENT session id, so /clear or /compact scatters one run across sibling dirs; toolUseResult.totalTokens is only the LAST API call's usage (measured 90,971 vs 1,235,241 summed — a 14x under-report) while totalDurationMs/toolStats/resolvedModel are trustworthy; there is no completion marker inside a transcript (measured healthy flush gaps up to 30s against a 180s harness stall threshold), so liveness must be three-state; spawnDepth is 1 for both direct and workflow subagents so it does not encode nesting; and workflow-agent user-retry/user-skip write nothing to disk, so a Touch-issued termination is indistinguishable from a crash unless Touch keeps its own control audit. The file ends with a per-lifecycle-stage table of exactly what an n8n-style graph may honestly assert at each moment, and the recommendation to render harness-derived structure and convention/declared structure as visually distinct layers — since the README's pause/terminate controls would otherwise sit on nodes the harness never confirmed.
- /home/laniakea/Projects/touch/.claude/local-orchestrators/touch-aggregator/findings/research-liveio-attempt-1.md — 20 findings on Touch's live path, all verified empirically against CLI 2.1.220, the running session (pid 622), and throwaway experiments in /tmp/claude-1000/liveio. Two blockers. (1) LIVEIO-1: there is NO way to attach to an already-running interactive Claude session — /proc/622/fd shows only /dev/pts/0, no unix socket exists until a background session is started, and daemon roster.json lists only daemon workers. Touch must OWN (spawn) every session it displays; README.md's "web view over claude code session" cannot mean mirroring the user's existing terminal. (2) LIVEIO-9: "pause" (README.md:6) does not exist anywhere in the CLI's control vocabulary — only interrupt, kill, stop_task and hook deny/block. Honest implementations are a blocking gate hook at SubagentStart/PreToolUse, or a cooperative control-file check inside the workflow script; both pause only at an agent boundary, which the UI must say. Restart is real and cheap: the Workflow runtime memoises agent() calls by prompt hash (journal key "v2:<sha256>"), so re-running with the same runId replays completed agents ("100% cache hit"). The big positive: I proved, twice, that a raw ANSI terminal stream with input, resize and kill is available locally — `<versioned-binary> --bg-pty-host <sock> <cols> <rows> -- <cmd> [args]` opens a unix socket with a 5-byte-header frame protocol (uint32BE len + uint8 kind; kind 0 = PTY bytes, kind 1 = JSON control), replays a 256KB scrollback ring then sends {"t":"live"}, and fans out to multiple subscribers. I drove a real interactive Claude REPL through it (36 frames, first at t+0.00s). Caveats: output is streamed to any connector unauthenticated (LIVEIO-3, and the input gate fails open when the tokens file is unreadable), and the interface is private/version-coupled (LIVEIO-4), so it needs a capability probe plus SDK stream-json as the declared fallback. For the graph page, hooks are decisive: all 31 hook events enumerated from the binary, every payload carries agent_id/agent_type, SubagentStart fires 70ms after spawn and SubagentStop hands over agent_transcript_path — but hooks are strictly blocking (measured: a sleep-3 PreToolUse hook added 3.10s to a 67ms tool; default timeout is 600s), so the hook must only append a line to a file. Transcript tailing is message-granular with 1-5s bursts and cannot back a terminal. The session registry has no heartbeat (622.json said status=busy with updatedAt 854s stale), so liveness must come from /proc+procStart or `claude agents --json`. Remote Control is an api.anthropic.com cloud relay and should be rejected.
- /home/laniakea/Projects/touch/.claude/local-orchestrators/touch-aggregator/findings/research-control-attempt-1.md — A "loop" is a JS program running via vm.runInContext inside ONE claude process — verified by ps (PID 622 only) while six workflow agents ran concurrently — so no loop, agent or attempt has an OS identity to signal. For an already-running interactive session there is NO external control transport at all: claude listens on no TCP port, stdin is /dev/pts/0 with dev.tty.legacy_tiocsti=0 (injection disabled), no control.sock exists without the bg daemon, and no custom signal handler exists beyond terminate. The only supported channel is --input-format stream-json, whose control_request parser accepts exactly initialize/interrupt/set_model/set_permission_mode — verified live (interrupt returned success and killed the in-flight background task). Of the README's four verbs: START is fully achievable (three routes; structured control and terminal fidelity cannot come from one process). TERMINATE is achievable, cleanly via interrupt, destructively via process kill (which also loses the workflows/<runId>.json completion record, written only at run end). RESTART exists only as Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — same-session only, a model-facing tool call, resumable only at agent() boundaries, with in-flight agents respawned from scratch and no working-tree rollback. PAUSE as specified does not exist: the harness's own "pause" (kft) is the same function as kill (tve) with a different status string. The one genuinely new finding is that hooks are a working external control plane — a PreToolUse HTTP hook verifiably held a tool call 20s then released it, and its payload carries agent_id/agent_type, so Touch can pause, step and gate a single agent while siblings run; the limits are tool-boundary latency, a 600000ms timeout ceiling, and deny being visible to the model. Notably, per-agent kill/pause/skip/retry already exist in-process (ISd/Vfr/zfr) but are wired only to the Ink TUI with no transport out. 17 findings written to the findings file, including a five-item list of what is semantically impossible.
- /home/laniakea/Projects/touch/.claude/local-orchestrators/touch-aggregator/findings/research-priorart-attempt-1.md — The existing monitoring module is a well-built read-only prototype whose craft should be mined and whose architecture cannot become Touch. Verified correct and worth reusing verbatim: torn-tail tailing with a truncation sentinel (monitor_server.py:330-356, decision_watcher.py:470-491), checkpoint-with-journal-identity plus atomic os.replace (:494-520), monotonic token deltas with message-id dedup (:154-197), /clear-/compact session-rotation path union (:86-100), realpath containment in safe_artifact_path (monitor_server.py:199-212), escape-first markdown + NODE_STATES whitelist discipline (monitor.html:299-321, 463-543), status.sh itself, and the query-string-as-state routing model.

Two blockers stop reuse-in-place. (1) The transport is one-directional by construction: handle() never parses the HTTP method or reads a request body, drain_client() exists purely to discard client frames, and unknown routes return the dashboard with 200 — there is nowhere to put a pause/start/terminate command or a terminal keystroke. (2) There is no authentication, Origin check, or Host check on a 0.0.0.0 bind; harmless for a read-only dashboard, but it makes the control plane CSRF-reachable from any browser tab the moment controls exist. Both must be designed before the first write endpoint.

Nine major scope breaks follow. The aggregation unit is a repo-local task folder, not a Claude Code session (~/.claude/sessions/*.json — sessionId/cwd/status/name/tempo/tmux — is never read, though it is exactly the sidebar model). Visibility is gated on the [monitor] prompt marker in one workflow journal, so ordinary session subagents (two exist in this session, with richer meta: agentType/description/toolUseId/spawnDepth) are invisible. Parallel fan-out is unrepresentable: the watcher builds labels from role+attempt and discards stage, so the six live researchers all read "research #1" and monitor.html:287 collapses them into ONE flow node — the exact case the n8n graph exists to show. The flat (plan, stage, state) schema has no node ids or edges and no version field, so it cannot be the graph source nor evolve over permanent history. agent_tokens() fully re-parses every running agent's whole transcript every second (measured 16 ms/2.26 MB at 6 min; ~300+ ms/tick extrapolated to a 2-hour run) on the thread that also tails the journal. Replay always starts at byte 0, one frame per event, with an untrimmed log DOM and a 500 ms full-resync option — measured ~1.5 MB/h of events, ≈3 MB/s per tab at an hour of history.

Control is where the prior art is structurally blind, and the CLI binary settles it: workflows are background tasks in a task registry, stopped with TaskStop({taskId}) and resumed with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — and the binary states stops "leave no transcript marker". So a paused run looks identical to a stalled one and the 60 s quiet debounce will fabricate a completion verdict for it; and a resume replays cached agent() calls into a NEW journal, which load_state() handles by resetting offset=0 and re-emitting the entire history into the same events.jsonl (duplicate rows and token deltas). The journal's per-spawn "key" content hash is the natural idempotency handle and is currently ignored. Finally, one watcher process watches exactly one run with all run identity in module globals, so N sessions x M runs needs a real ~800-line refactor into per-run objects plus a supervisor, not a wrapper.

Minor items: unknown ?task= silently streams a different task instead of 404; no method dispatch or 404 at all; multi-writer append safety rests on an undocumented one-write()-per-record invariant (proved: 0/800 corrupted with one write per record, 206/800 when a record spans two writes — so Touch must not carry terminal output over a shared append file); reserved magic names share the namespace with runtime-generated ids; classify() sleeps in the poll thread (~9 s stall on a 6-way fan-out); and the network layer has zero tests while the frontend is tested by grepping its own source — a posture that must be decided globally now (stdlib socket-level integration tests keep zero-dependency; a JS runner does not).
- /home/laniakea/Projects/touch/.claude/local-orchestrators/touch-aggregator/findings/research-stack-attempt-1.md — Stack/delivery research for Touch, verified empirically on this machine (probes in /tmp/claude-1000; nothing written to the live task folder except the two mandated status.sh calls and the findings file). 18 findings: 3 blockers, 9 major, 6 minor.

Two premises in the brief turned out to be false and change the design. (1) The firewall does NOT block package installs: `npm install @xterm/xterm dagre elkjs cytoscape mermaid` and a pip dry-run both succeeded through the CONNECT proxy. The real constraint is runtime offline-safety — the browser loading the page (especially from the host after `sbx ports --publish`) gets no proxy, so nothing may be fetched at page load. Rule to codify: stdlib-only at runtime, npm allowed only to vendor pinned, committed assets (note .gitignore:18-19 ignores node_modules/ and dist/, so vendored files must live at touch-visual/vendor/). (2) `node-pty` cannot build here — no g++ in the image (`make: g++: No such file or directory`), while Python's stdlib `pty` works end-to-end including TIOCSWINSZ resize, so the PTY tier must be Python.

Blockers. No local control channel exists on a running CLI: `messagingSocketPath` is emitted undefined in the 2.1.220 binary, no session sockets exist on disk, and `--remote-control` is an Anthropic cloud bridge (`/v1/sessions`, "will not appear in the Claude app"). Touch can only drive sessions it spawns itself; every other session is read-only transcript replay, and the sidebar must show the two classes differently. Spawning is booby-trapped: a `claude` launched from inside an agent session inherits `CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1` and prints "Transcript saving is off" — verified live, and verified fixed by scrubbing CLAUDE*/AI_AGENT from the child env — which would silently starve the entire graph half of data. And the existing server binds 0.0.0.0 with no auth and never reads the Origin header: a probe handshake with `Origin: http://evil.example` got a 101, so adding keystroke input to that socket is cross-origin RCE against a session running --dangerously-skip-permissions with ~/.claude/.credentials.json readable.

Transport/terminal. The existing WS cannot receive: `parse_client_frames` deletes payloads without unmasking (monitor_server.py:307) and a masked client frame is silently dropped (verified). The 0.5s poll (monitor_server.py:378) is a latency floor no terminal survives; the verified alternative is `pty.openpty()` + `Popen(start_new_session=True)` + `loop.add_reader` inside asyncio (never `pty.fork()`). Captured bytes from a real claude TUI include alt-screen, mouse 1000/1002/1003/1006, bracketed paste, DA1 identification queries and 24-bit color, so xterm.js (489KB UMD + 7KB CSS) is required — hand-rolling means dropping the terminal-fidelity requirement. For the graph, do not vendor a layout engine (dagre.min 284KB, elk 1.6MB, cytoscape 435KB, mermaid 84MB installed): the loop DAG's ranks are fixed by the two workflow templates and monitor.html:296-318 already prototypes the flow strip — hand-roll layered SVG with stable node ids so updates patch rather than re-layout.

Control. Loop restart is an in-session `Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId})` tool call (binary strings, plus "completed agents return cached results") — there is no external API, so buttons must be queued, acknowledged intents gated on `status: idle` from ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json, with honest verb definitions. Terminate needs an escalation ladder: SIGTERM was verified to leave an interactive TUI running; SIGHUP/closing the master and SIGKILL work, EOT exits cleanly. A real local PTY-socket surface does exist for background agents (/tmp/cc-daemon-1000/<id>/{control.sock,pty/<id>.sock}, hard-coded 200x50) — documented as deliberately not used, since it is undocumented and version-coupled.

Also: key sessions on (pid, procStart) — procStart equals /proc/<pid>/stat field 22, verified — since sessionId rotates on /clear; the registry keeps ghosts for a passive reader while `claude agents --json` (0.65s, supported, TTY-free) prunes them; expose typed projected endpoints over ~/.claude rather than any path parameter; poll at 250ms (0.39ms per full scan, no stdlib inotify); one process on one port (default 8932, since 8931 is the live monitor); and put app source at repo root as aggregator/, touch-visual/, tests/ with a run_all.sh, keeping .gitignore edits additive so test_shell.py:155 keeps passing.

DRIVER CONTEXT (read this SECOND, in full — it is REQUIRED input):
/home/laniakea/Projects/touch/.claude/local-orchestrators/touch-aggregator/context/driver-context.md
The research agents ran BLIND on purpose: they never saw that file, so their

- execute-research: Research a codebase or any source from multiple read-only perspectives and synthesize ONE complete implementation plan (no sub-plans — implement-plan divides it). Use when asked to research / investigate / analyze something and produce a plan; pass the user's request as the argument.
- implement-plan: Take the complete plan produced by execute-research (or an equivalent plan), divide it into isolated feature-sub-plans via a Fable divider agent, then implement them through generated, monitored implement→test→critique loops (serial by default). Use when asked to execute / implement a plan; pass the user's request as the argument.
- m-orchestrator: Plug live websocket monitoring into a deterministic orchestrator (Workflow script or any agent-spawning driver). Use when building or running multi-agent orchestrations that need live per-plan progress, orchestrator decision tracing, and token accounting on a browser dashboard. Provides generic scripts in .claude/shared/monitoring/ plus the integration protocol.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

51	## SESSIONDATA-1 — `usage` is duplicated on every split assistant record; naive summing over-counts tokens 2.09x

53	**Proof / severity:** `blocker`.

55	lines 10, 11, 13 (one API response, `requestId` `req_011CdMzWfroAZexCFHM4FjYy`,

80	## SESSIONDATA-2 — thinking text is never persisted: every `thinking` block on disk has `thinking: ""`

113	## SESSIONDATA-3 — the transcript is **not** append-only: the CLI truncates and whole-file-rewrites it. Byte-offset tailing will break.
114	
115	**Proof / severity:** `blocker` for any offset-based tailer.
116	Binary offset 259265400 onwards, class `wsp`:
117	
118	- `performRemoveByUuid(e,t)` opens the file `r+`, reads the last `xI` (64 KiB),
119	  finds `"uuid":"<uuid>"`, then `await n.truncate(A)` and rewrites the tail
120	  after the removed line. **The file shrinks.** If the uuid is not in the last
121	  64 KiB and the file is under `ZF_` (50 MiB), it falls back to
122	  `readFile → filter → writeFile` — a full rewrite. Over 50 MiB it logs
123	  "Skipping tombstone removal: session file too large" and gives up.
124	- `performCompactTranscript(e)` writes `${file}.compact.tmp.${randomBytes(4).hex}`
125	  and renames over the original, **dropping every line before the
126	  `compact_boundary` except the preserved segment**. It is armed when
127	  `bytesSinceCompact >= 20971520` and the file is `>= 5242880` bytes.
128	  Currently gated by `Z2o = !1` (off), but `Z2o` has a setter, so it can be
129	  turned on by a config/gate flip in any release or remotely.
130	
131	**Scenario:** Touch's aggregator tails from a saved byte offset. A user hits
132	esc-esc / rewinds / deletes a message; the file shrinks below the saved offset;
133	the reader's next `seek(offset)` reads garbage or nothing and the terminal pane
134	silently freezes for the rest of the session. Under the compaction gate, the
135	same thing happens with no user action at all.
136	
137	**Recommendation:** never trust a bare byte offset. Persist
138	`(st_dev, st_ino, size, offset)`; on every poll, if inode changed **or**
139	`size < offset`, discard state and re-read the file from 0. Key every record by
140	`uuid` and make the in-memory model idempotent on re-ingest (upsert-by-uuid,
141	not append), so a full re-read is a no-op for the UI. Handle
142	`<file>.compact.tmp.*` appearing next to the transcript as "rewrite in flight —
143	back off 200ms and re-read".

147	## SESSIONDATA-4 — `mode`, `permission-mode`, `ai-title`, `last-prompt` etc. are re-appended state, not events
148	
149	**Proof / severity:** `major`.

151	`ai-title` ×15 — for a session whose mode never changed. The binary
152	(`planReAppendSessionMetadata`, offset ~259270500) re-appends the current value

173	## SESSIONDATA-5 — writes are batched (100 ms) into a single large append; torn tails are guaranteed, and latency is ~100 ms
174	
175	**Proof / severity:** `major` (correctness) — and a *positive* result on latency.
176	
177	Latency, measured live: a polling loop started inside a Bash tool call saw the
178	`assistant`/`tool_use` record **for that very call** land **+0.10 s** after the
179	poll began (`timestamp 2026-07-25T03:01:33.485Z`), i.e. before the tool had
180	finished. So intra-turn visibility is real and sub-second — good enough to drive
181	a live view without any extra instrumentation.

183	Correctness: `drainQueuesOnce` (binary, offset ~259268400) concatenates queued
184	entries into one string `o` and issues **one** `gc.appendFile(e, o)` per batch,
185	splitting only at `MAX_CHUNK_BYTES = 104857600` (100 MiB). Observed max line
186	length in this project: 46 567 bytes (`agent-a82d2e2591c84a3d7.jsonl`),
187	38 899 bytes in the main transcript. A reader polling every 100–250 ms will
188	routinely observe a batch mid-write.
189	
190	**Scenario:** the aggregator reads to EOF and `json.loads` the last chunk;
191	it raises on a half-written 46 KB line, and (if the reader advances its offset

193	never completed.
194	
195	**Recommendation:** read to EOF, cut the buffer at the **last** `\n`, keep the
196	remainder in memory for the next poll, and advance the offset only by the
197	consumed prefix. Decode with `errors="ignore"`/incremental decoder — a cut can
198	land mid-UTF-8. `decision_watcher.py:471` (`read whole journal lines appended

62	## AGENTGRAPH-1 — Journal entries have no timestamps, and journal ORDER is not spawn order
63	
64	- **Proof**: `/home/agent/.claude/projects/-home-laniakea-Projects-touch/dd469822-2546-47d9-aaa3-31db4cb705e8/subagents/workflows/wf_829e6f58-b2f/journal.jsonl:1-6` (no `ts` field anywhere), and binary offset `255829400` (`a.append({type:"started",key:…,agentId:…})` — three fields, no clock).
65	- **Severity**: major
66	
67	Journal append order for the 6-way `parallel()` fan-out was
68	`a2fc, a74f, a9ea, a82d, a79f, a2ec`. The true spawn order, taken from each
69	transcript's first-line `timestamp`, is
70	`a2fc(.846), a82d(.849), a74f(.850), a9ea(.851), a2ec(.852), a79f(.852)`.
71	Two agents even share a millisecond. So journal position is an append race, not
72	a causal or temporal order.
73	
74	**Scenario**: Touch lays out an n8n graph left-to-right by journal line number.
75	On every parallel fan-out the columns are shuffled relative to reality, and any
76	"who started first" annotation is wrong. Worse, if Touch ever derives edges
77	("A then B") from adjacency in the journal, it invents causality that does not
78	exist.

80	**Recommendation**: treat `journal.jsonl` strictly as an unordered *set* of
81	facts `(key → agentId)` and `(key → result)`. Every timestamp on a node must
82	come from the agent transcript: spawn = first parseable `timestamp` in
83	`agent-<id>.jsonl`; last activity = last parseable `timestamp`. Order sibling
84	nodes by that spawn timestamp, and when two spawn times are within the same
85	millisecond, fall back to a stable tiebreak (agentId) rather than pretending to
86	know. `decision_watcher.py:244-302` (`first_ts` / `last_ts`) already implements
87	exactly this and is the right model to copy.

528	## AGENTGRAPH-17 — What an n8n-style graph can HONESTLY show at each moment (the summary this perspective owes)
529	
530	- **Proof**: the composite of AGENTGRAPH-1..16; the reconstruction recipe below
531	  was validated against the live run.
532	- **Severity**: major (this is the design decision the plan must make explicitly)
533	
534	**Reconstruction recipe (unconditional harness data only)**
535	
536	| Graph element | Source | Unconditional? |
537	|---|---|---|
538	| Session node | `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<sessionId>.jsonl` + `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` | yes |
539	| Session → Agent-tool subagent edge | parent `tool_use` (`name:"Agent"`, `id`) ↔ `meta.toolUseId` | yes |
540	| Agent-tool node label | `tool_use.input.description` / `meta.description` | yes |
541	| Session → Workflow node edge | parent `toolUseResult` `{runId, transcriptDir, scriptPath, workflowName}` | yes |
542	| Workflow → agent edge | file lives in `subagents/workflows/<runId>/` | yes |
543	| Nested agent edge (depth ≥ 2) | `meta.parentAgentId` | yes |
544	| Node spawn time | first `timestamp` in `agent-<id>.jsonl` | yes |
545	| Node last-activity | last parseable `timestamp` in `agent-<id>.jsonl` | yes |
546	| Node completion | journal `result` for its `key` / parent `tool_result` | yes |
547	| Node tokens | Σ `message.usage` over transcript, dedup by `message.id` | yes |
548	| Node tool count / duration | `toolUseResult.totalToolUseCount`, `.totalDurationMs` (Agent tool only) | yes |
549	| Node **role / plan / attempt / phase** | `[monitor]` marker in prompt | **NO — convention** |
550	| Node **label / phase title / index** | `<runId>.json` `workflowProgress[]`, at run END only | no (late) |
551	| **Queued** nodes | nothing | **NO — must be declared** |
552	| **Loop / retry grouping** | journal `key` (harness) + marker `attempt` (convention) | mixed |
553	
554	**Honest lifecycle rendering**
555	
556	- *Before launch*: only declared nodes (from the seeded `status.sh … queued`
557	  events or a parsed script). Style them as declarations.
558	- *T+0 to first transcript flush (~200 ms observed: workflow launched
559	  02:59:29.624, first agent transcript line 02:59:29.846)*: journal `started`
560	  lines may exist before the transcript is readable —
561	  `decision_watcher.py:330-367` retries classification 3× at 0.5 s and falls
562	  through to "pending" rather than blocking. Touch needs the same: a node can be
563	  known-to-exist but unnamed for a second.
564	- *During the run*: nodes have identity (agentId), parent, spawn time, live
565	  token/last-activity, and — only if the orchestrator embedded the marker — role,
566	  plan and attempt. State is `running` or `unknown/idle Ns`. Edges between
567	  sibling agents (the "loop" arrows impl→test→critique) are **not** in any
568	  harness data; they are implied by the orchestrator script's control flow and
569	  must be drawn from the marker's `plan`+`stage`, i.e. convention.
570	- *At each result*: the node gets a verdict shape. The verdict semantics
571	  (`passed`/`approved`/`files_changed`/`findings`) come from the workflow's
572	  schemas (`implement.workflow.js:45-61`), not the harness —
573	  `decision_watcher.py:370-447` already encodes exactly this shape-driven
574	  mapping and is the right thing to reuse.
575	- *At run end*: reconcile against `<runId>.json` to fill in authoritative
576	  `index`, `label`, `phaseTitle`, `attempt`, `durationMs`, `status`
577	  (`completed|failed|killed`), `totalTokens`, `totalToolCalls`. Only after this
578	  can Touch claim the graph is complete — and only if the snapshot exists.
579	
580	**Recommendation**: write this table into Touch's data-model design as a
581	first-class contract, and make the UI encode the harness/convention split
582	visually (e.g. solid nodes+edges for harness-derived facts, dashed for
583	convention-derived or declared structure). The README asks for a graph that also
584	*controls* loops; a control surface built on convention-derived structure that
585	looks identical to harness-derived structure is how a user ends up terminating
586	the wrong node.
587

591	
592	`research.workflow.js` produces a graph of exactly
593	`len(PERSPECTIVES)` parallel nodes → barrier → 1 synthesis node
594	(`research.workflow.js:136-153`). `implement.workflow.js` produces
595	`1 divide node → per sub-plan { impl → test → critique }×attempts → finalgate
596	{ gate → fix }×2` (`implement.workflow.js:163-210, 255-349`), serial by default.

111	## LIVEIO-3 — The PTY socket streams output to *anyone* who connects; only input is token-gated
112	
113	**Severity: major (security)**
114	**Proof:** `/tmp/claude-1000/liveio/ptytest2.py`, run against a live socket:
115	```
116	NOAUTH ctrl frames: [hello, live, ping, {"t":"auth-required"}]   # ← full scrollback
117	                                                                  #   arrived before this
118	AUTH  (token from roster.json ptyAuth) → input echoed back
119	```
120	`auth-required` is only emitted **after** the client tries to write a DATA frame;
121	`hello` + scrollback + live data are sent unconditionally. The binary also
122	contains `tokens-file unreadable; DATA gate fail-open`, i.e. a missing token file
123	disables the input gate entirely rather than closing it.
124	
125	**Scenario.** Touch bridges this socket to a WebSocket on `0.0.0.0:<port>`
126	(mandatory in this sandbox — CLAUDE.md:112-114). Anyone who can reach that port
127	now has (a) the full transcript of the user's session rendered as text, and (b)
128	if Touch forwards keystrokes, an unauthenticated shell inside the sandbox with
129	`--dangerously-skip-permissions` on. The published-port model means "reachable"
130	is not just localhost.
131	
132	**Recommendation.** Non-negotiables for the bridge: create the socket in a
133	`0700` directory Touch owns; always set `CLAUDE_BG_PTY_AUTH` to a fresh random
134	secret per session and keep it server-side (never send it to the browser);
135	require a Touch-issued session token on the WebSocket **before** relaying any
136	frame in either direction; make input relaying opt-in per connection so a
137	read-only viewer cannot type. Also decide explicitly whether the browser may
138	send `{"t":"kill"}` — that is a remote process kill.

253	## LIVEIO-7 — Hooks are strictly blocking; a slow hook stalls the user's session (default timeout 600 s)
254	
255	**Severity: major (cost)**
256	**Proof — measured.** Same prompt, with an extra `sleep 3` command added to the
257	`PreToolUse` matcher (`/tmp/claude-1000/liveio/settings2.json`):
258	```
259	0.00 SessionStart
260	0.47 UserPromptSubmit
261	2.75 PreToolUse   Bash
262	5.85 PostToolUse  Bash   toolms=67      ← 3.10 s wall for a 67 ms tool
263	7.33 MessageDisplay
264	7.39 Stop
265	```
266	Default timeout: `var Hm=600000` (10 minutes), used as `timeoutMs:i=Hm` in the
267	hook executor `lM`. Hooks under one event run and are all awaited before the
268	turn continues; when no hook matches the executor returns immediately
269	(`if(y.length===0)return`), so unconfigured events cost nothing.
270	
271	**Scenario.** Touch's hook does an HTTP POST to its own aggregator. The
272	aggregator is down / the sandbox proxy 403s / the port moved. Every tool call in
273	the user's session now blocks for the socket timeout, and with the default the
274	session can appear frozen for ten minutes with no UI explanation.
275	
276	**Recommendation.** The hook must be `append one line to a local file and exit` —

315	## LIVEIO-9 — "Pause" does not exist in any channel; the README control set must be redefined before it is built
316	
317	**Severity: blocker (product/spec)**
318	**Proof:** README.md:5-6 requires "pause, restart, start and terminate agents
319	loops". The complete control vocabulary available is:
320	`interrupt`, `stop_task`, `agents_killed`, `set_permission_mode`, `set_model`,
321	`set_cwd`, `rewind_files`, … (`subtype:v.literal(...)` enumeration above), plus
322	PTY `{"t":"kill"}` and hook decisions
323	(`permissionDecision: allow|deny|ask` for PreToolUse; `decision: approve|block`
324	+ `continue:false` + `stopReason` for Stop/SubagentStop —
325	`grep -aoE 'decision:v\.enum\(\["approve","block"\]'`). There is **no** suspend
326	or resume anywhere. The loops themselves are plain `while` loops in a Workflow
327	script (`implement.workflow.js:168`, `research.workflow.js`) — the runtime has no
328	notion of a pausable step.
329	
330	What each verb can honestly mean:
331	- **start** — Touch spawns the session/workflow (LIVEIO-2). Real.
332	- **terminate** — PTY `{"t":"kill","sig":"SIGTERM"}`, or `control_request
333	  interrupt` in SDK mode, or `claude stop <short>` for a bg agent (I ran it:
334	  `stopped 8084340e`). Real, but coarse: it kills the whole run, not one loop.
335	- **restart** — real, and better than expected: the Workflow runtime memoises
336	  each `agent()` call by prompt hash. `journal.jsonl` lines are
337	  `{"type":"started","key":"v2:<sha256>","agentId":…}` and the binary says
338	  *"completed agents return cached results … 100% cache hit"*. Re-running the
339	  same script with the same `runId` replays finished agents and re-runs only what
340	  is missing.
341	- **pause** — does not exist. `SIGSTOP` on the process is not a substitute: it
342	  freezes mid-HTTP-stream and the API request will time out, so "resume" resumes
343	  into a broken turn.
344	
345	**Recommendation.** Two honest implementations, pick one and label the button
346	accordingly:
347	1. **Gate hook (works for any session, no script change).** A `SubagentStart`
348	   (or `PreToolUse`) hook that blocks while a control file says "paused". This is
349	   a *real* pause with a real resume, bounded by the hook `timeout` — set it
350	   explicitly (e.g. 300 s) and have the hook release-and-report when it expires,
351	   so a forgotten pause degrades to "resumed" rather than to a wedged session.
352	   UI must say **"pause at next agent boundary"**, not "pause".
353	2. **Cooperative check in the orchestrator script.** `implement.workflow.js:74`
354	   already does `const fs = await import('node:fs')`, so the loop can poll a
355	   control file between `agent()` calls and also honour an "abort" flag. This
356	   gives pause/abort at a semantically meaningful boundary and needs no hook, but
357	   only works for loops Touch generated.
358	   (Note the workflow sandbox forbids `Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date()` —
359	   the control file must carry any timestamp the script needs.)
360	
361	Whatever is chosen, the graph page must render the *pending* state ("pause
362	requested — will take effect at the next agent boundary"), because the gap
363	between click and effect is one whole agent, i.e. minutes.

439	present: `pid, sessionId, cwd, startedAt, procStart, version, peerProtocol, kind,

1	# Research findings — THE CONTROL PLANE
2	
3	Perspective: *can an external web page start, pause, restart or terminate agent
4	loops?* Everything below was verified against primary sources on this machine
5	(running processes, `~/.claude` on-disk state, the 2.1.220 CLI binary, and two
6	throwaway live experiments under `/tmp/claude-1000`). Where a claim rests on an
7	experiment, the exact command/script path is given.

10	
11	## Part 0 — What a "loop" IS at runtime (the premise everything else rests on)
12	
13	Established by reading the skill templates plus the live run of this very
14	research task:
15	
16	1. **A loop is a JavaScript program, not a process.**
17	   `.claude/skills/implement-plan/templates/implement.workflow.js:163-210`
18	   (`runLoop`) is a `while (!success && attempt < MAX_ATTEMPTS)` loop that
19	   `await`s three `agent()` calls. `execute-research`'s "loop" is flatter —
20	   `research.workflow.js:139-144` is one `parallel()` fan-out plus a barrier,
21	   then one synthesizer (`:150`). There is no daemon, no queue, no scheduler.
22	2. **The script runs inside the CLI process, in a `vm` context.**
23	   Binary: `tEd=S(()=>{…Msn=x(require("vm"))})` and
24	   `let d; try { p = e.runInContext(l.vmContext…` — the workflow source is
25	   compiled and run with `vm.runInContext` inside the same Node process.
26	3. **Its agents are also in-process.** Verified: `ps -eo pid,ppid,stat,args`
27	   while six workflow researchers were concurrently live showed exactly **one**
28	   `claude` process (`PID 622`) and no child `claude`/`node` processes; every
29	   `agent-*.jsonl` under
30	   `~/.claude/projects/-home-laniakea-Projects-touch/dd469822-…/subagents/workflows/wf_829e6f58-b2f/`
31	   is written by PID 622, and every Bash call an agent makes has `PPID 622`.
32	4. **The only durable, resumable boundary is one `agent()` call.** The run dir
33	   holds `journal.jsonl` with one line per agent lifecycle event:
34	   `{"type":"started","key":"v2:<sha256>","agentId":"a2fc883c96ff7b837"}` and a
35	   later `{"type":"result",…}`. The Workflow tool's own doc string in the binary
36	   states it exactly:
37	
38	   > "To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with
39	   > `Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId})` — the longest unchanged prefix of
40	   > `agent()` calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call
41	   > and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit."
42	
43	   and `resumeFromRunId` is documented as *"Completed agent() calls with
44	   unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited
45	   or new calls re-run. **Same-session only.** Stop the prior run first before
46	   resuming."*
47	5. **In-flight agents are re-run, not resumed.** The binary emits telemetry
48	   `tengu_workflow_journal_started_hit_respawn` when replay finds a `started`
49	   key with no matching `result` — i.e. an agent that was aborted mid-flight is
50	   spawned again from scratch. Our live journal proves the shape: at the time of
51	   writing it contains six `started` lines and zero `result` lines.

86	- `/proc/622/fd/0 -> /dev/pts/0`, `fd/1 -> /dev/pts/0` — stdin is a PTY *slave*.
87	  Writing to the slave paints the screen; it does not inject input.

497	## CONTROL-16 — `TaskStop` and `Workflow` are model-facing tools; any Touch verb built on them is advisory, not deterministic
498	**Evidence:** `TaskStop` schema (in-session tool, `task_id`); the current run's
499	task id `wpbwj76b3` appears only in the tool result inside the session
500	transcript; `Workflow` is likewise a tool. Both require an assistant turn.
501	Additionally `Workflow` can be disabled outright: `disableWorkflows` managed
502	setting, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS`, the `/config` "Dynamic workflows"
503	toggle, and a named-workflows-only mode that rejects `script`/`scriptPath`/
504	`resumeFromRunId`/`remote`.

506	
507	**Scenario.** Touch's "terminate loop" sends the adopted session a turn saying
508	"call TaskStop with wpbwj76b3". The model is mid-tool-call, or decides to ask a
509	clarifying question, or the session has workflows disabled by policy — and the
510	loop keeps running while the UI shows "terminating".
511	
512	**Recommendation.** Every model-mediated verb in Touch must be modelled as a
513	**request with an observable confirmation**: issue → watch the deterministic
514	signal (journal `started`/`result`, `SubagentStop` hook, `task_updated` event)
515	→ only then flip the UI state, with a visible timeout and a fallback to the
516	deterministic path (`interrupt`). Also probe workflow availability at session

521	## CONTROL-17 — What is semantically impossible (state this in the plan, don't discover it in sprint 3)
522	**Evidence:** the union of CONTROL-1/2/4/5/9/11.
523	**Severity: major** (scope-defining).
524	
525	1. **Suspend/resume of in-flight model inference.** No primitive exists at any
526	   layer. The nearest approximations are: freeze the OS process (CONTROL-11,
527	   whole session, risky) or gate at tool boundaries (CONTROL-8, granular,
528	   delayed). Neither preserves an in-progress turn against a real abort.
529	2. **Pausing one loop while its siblings continue — at process level.** They are
530	   the same process (CONTROL-1). Only the hook gate achieves it, and only at
531	   tool boundaries.
532	3. **Resuming a workflow into a different session.** `resumeFromRunId` is
533	   same-session only. If the CLI process dies, that run's remaining `agent()`
534	   calls can never be resumed by the harness — a new session can only re-launch
535	   the script (the journal *cache* is keyed by prompt, but the resume entry
536	   point is session-scoped).
537	4. **Controlling a session Touch did not start.** No writable channel exists
538	   (CONTROL-2). Read-only + `kill(pid)` is the complete achievable set.
539	5. **Undoing an aborted agent's file edits.** Not a harness concern at all
540	   (CONTROL-7); if Touch doesn't checkpoint, nobody does.
541	
542	**Recommendation.** Put a "Control semantics" table in the plan's global
543	decisions section with exactly four rows — start / pause / restart / terminate —
544	each stating: the mechanism, the granularity (session vs run vs agent), what
545	happens to in-flight work, what happens on disk, and whether it is deterministic
546	or model-mediated. Every UI control must map to one row; anything that maps to
547	none gets cut from the README rather than half-built.

17	## PRIORART-1 — The transport is one-directional by construction; there is no place to put a control command
18	
19	**File**: `.claude/shared/monitoring/monitor_server.py:393-514` (`handle`),
20	`:313-327` (`drain_client`), `:358-388` (`stream_events`)
21	**Severity**: blocker
22	
23	**Scenario.** Touch's per-terminal page must "pause, restart, start and
24	terminate agent loops" (README.md:5-6) and the main page must accept keystrokes
25	into a live Claude Code session (README.md:3-4). Nothing in the prior art can
26	carry a byte from browser to backend:
27	
28	- `handle()` parses the request line at `:403-404` but **never reads the HTTP
29	  method** and never reads a request body (it stops at `readuntil(b"\r\n\r\n")`,
30	  `:397`). A `POST /control` is indistinguishable from `GET /control`.
31	- The websocket is server→client only: `drain_client()` (`:313-327`) exists
32	  purely to *discard* client frames and detect CLOSE. `parse_client_frames()`
33	  (`:279-310`) deliberately skips over payloads without ever decoding them —
34	  it does not even unmask.
35	- Every route that is not `/ws`, `/health`, `/tasks`, `/artifacts`, `/file`
36	  falls through to the catch-all that returns `monitor.html` with **200**
37	  (`:495-506`).
38	
39	The data model has the same shape: `events.jsonl` is append-only and every
40	consumer (`read_frames`, `task_status`, the browser) is a pure reader.
41	
42	**Recommendation.** Do not "add a POST endpoint" to `monitor_server.py` — its
43	request loop has no method dispatch, no body reader, no routing table, and no
44	keep-alive (every response hard-codes `Connection: close`). Keep the *reader*
45	half (tail + replay + WS framing) as a component, and put commands on a
46	separate, explicitly-designed plane. Migration consequence: the reader half is
47	~120 lines of `monitor_server.py` (`ws_frame`, `parse_client_frames`,
48	`drain_client`, `read_frames`, `stream_events`) and lifts cleanly; the
49	`handle()` router does not and should be replaced.

53	## PRIORART-2 — Zero authentication, no Origin check, no Host check, binds 0.0.0.0 — safe for a read-only dashboard, fatal the moment controls exist
54	
55	**File**: `monitor_server.py:519` (`asyncio.start_server(handle, "0.0.0.0", PORT)`),
56	`:412-441` (the entire `/ws` admission check)
57	**Severity**: blocker
58	
59	**Scenario.** The `/ws` upgrade validates exactly two things:
60	`sec-websocket-key` present and `sec-websocket-version in (None, "13")`. There
61	is no `Origin` validation, no `Host` allowlist, no token, no cookie, no
62	same-origin requirement. WebSocket connections are **not** subject to CORS, so
63	any web page the user visits in the same browser can today do
64	`new WebSocket("ws://<sandbox-host>:8931/ws?task=<name>")` and read the entire
65	event stream, and `fetch("/file?task=…&path=…")` to read every `.md`/`.html`
66	under a task folder (opaque-response restrictions do not apply to the WS path).
67	A `Host:`-header-based DNS-rebinding attack is likewise unblocked.
68	
69	Today the blast radius is "an attacker learns your agent logs". Once the same
70	origin accepts *pause/terminate/start* commands and terminal keystrokes, the
71	blast radius becomes **arbitrary command execution in the user's repo**, and it
72	is reachable by CSRF from any tab. The environment makes this worse, not
73	better: the module is documented to bind `0.0.0.0` and be published to the host
74	(`CLAUDE.md:112-114`).
75	
76	**Recommendation.** Decide the auth model **before** writing the first write
77	endpoint, not after: a per-boot random token in the URL (`/?k=<token>`) that the
78	page echoes into the WS query + an `Origin`/`Host` allowlist enforced in the
79	upgrade handler is the minimum, and is ~20 lines. Migration consequence: the
80	token must be printed on stdout at startup (the module already prints its state
81	dir at `:523-525`, so the pattern exists) and every `sbx ports --publish`
82	instruction in the docs must carry it.
83

171	## PRIORART-5 — Parallel fan-out is unrepresentable: six live agents render as six identical rows and collapse into ONE graph node
172	
173	**File**: `decision_watcher.py:636-638` and `:682-688` (label construction),
174	`monitor.html:287-293` (`upsertAgent` role derivation), `:300-321` (`renderFlow`)
175	**Proof**: `.claude/local-orchestrators/touch-aggregator/events.jsonl:12,15,17,19,21,23`
176	**Severity**: major
177	
178	**Scenario.** The watcher builds every agent label as
179	`f"{info['role']} #{info['attempt']}"` — role and attempt only. It **has**
180	`info["stage"]` in hand (it uses it as the emitted event's stage on the very
181	same line) and throws it away. For a `parallel()` fan-out every sibling shares
182	role and attempt, so every label is identical. From the live run right now:
183	
184	```
185	events.jsonl:12  "stage":"sessiondata" … "agent":{"id":"a2fc883c","label":"research #1"…}
186	events.jsonl:15  "stage":"liveio"      … "agent":{"id":"a74f0c93","label":"research #1"…}
187	events.jsonl:17  "stage":"control"     … "agent":{"id":"a9eabf26","label":"research #1"…}
188	events.jsonl:19  "stage":"agentgraph"  … "agent":{"id":"a82d2e25","label":"research #1"…}
189	events.jsonl:21  "stage":"stack"       … "agent":{"id":"a79fa2f4","label":"research #1"…}
190	events.jsonl:23  "stage":"priorart"    … "agent":{"id":"a2ec1069","label":"research #1"…}
191	```
192	
193	The frontend renders `a.label || a.id` into `.alabel` (`monitor.html:278`) and
194	never shows the id, so the user sees six rows all reading `research #1`. Worse,
195	the flow strip derives its node key by `(a.label||a.id).split(" #")[0]`
196	(`:287`) → all six map to the single role `"research"` → `renderFlow` draws
197	**one** node. The orchestrator log is equally degenerate: six consecutive
198	identical `"spawn research research attempt 1"` lines (`events.jsonl:11,14,16,
199	18,20,22`).
200	
201	This is precisely the case Touch's n8n-style graph exists to show.
202	
203	**Recommendation.** Two-line fix in the watcher: label as
204	`f"{info['stage']}:{info['role']} #{info['attempt']}"`, and add explicit
205	`agent.stage` / `agent.role` / `agent.attempt` fields to the `agent` sub-object
206	rather than making the UI reverse-engineer them out of a display string.
207	Migration consequence: purely additive to the event schema — already-recorded
208	history (which the ops rules forbid deleting, `CLAUDE.md:118-121`) still renders,
209	just with the old collapsed labels.

213	## PRIORART-6 — The event schema is a flat state overlay; it cannot express a graph, and it has no version field
214	
215	**File**: `.claude/shared/monitoring/monitoring.md:25-46` (normative schema),
216	`monitor.html:203-219` (`planEl` — one card per `plan` id)
217	**Severity**: major
218	
219	**Scenario.** The whole model is `(plan, stage, state)` → one card per `plan`,
220	one chip per `stage`, plus a per-agent row list. There are **no node ids, no
221	edges, no parent/child, no ordering other than first-seen**. `renderFlow`
222	(`monitor.html:300-321`) fakes a topology by iterating `p.roles` in insertion
223	order and drawing `→` between consecutive entries — that is a rendering
224	accident, not data. An n8n-like UML graph needs an actual node/edge structure
225	(fan-out, barrier/join, retry back-edge, gate branch), and none of it can be
226	derived from this stream.
227	
228	Separately: events carry **no schema version**. Backward compatibility so far
229	has been achieved by defaulting missing keys (`ev.tokens.cached || 0`,
230	`monitor.html:371`; the one-time backfill at `decision_watcher.py:538-561`).
231	Any *structural* change is unabsorbable, and the operating rule is that
232	completed runs' `events.jsonl` are permanent history that replays on connect
233	(`monitoring.md:183-187`).
234	
235	**Recommendation.** (a) Derive the graph topology from a source that actually
236	has one — the workflow script's phase/`agent()` structure plus the journal's
237	spawn order and the session transcript's Task parent/child edges — and use
238	events only to *paint state onto* nodes. (b) Add `"v": 2` to every emitted
239	event now, and have readers treat a missing `v` as 1. Migration consequence:
240	one field in `emit()` (`decision_watcher.py:138-152`) and in `status.sh:34-40`;
241	doing it later means either a lossy history migration or a permanent branch in
242	the reader.

246	## PRIORART-7 — The watcher fully re-parses every running agent's entire transcript once per second (O(size) per tick, and size grows all run)
247	
248	**File**: `decision_watcher.py:154-197` (`agent_tokens`), `:86-100`
249	(`agent_paths`), called from `:764-795` (every ~1s) and `:678`, `:705`
250	**Severity**: major
251	
252	**Scenario.** `agent_tokens(aid)` globs
253	`~/.claude/projects/*/*/subagents/workflows/<wf>/agent-<id>.jsonl` (a filesystem
254	glob, per agent, per tick) and then reads and `json.loads`-es **every line of
255	every copy** to rebuild `usage_by_msg` from scratch. It is called for every
256	still-running agent on every 1-second poll, and again on every result.
257	
258	Measured on the live run (`/tmp/claude-1000/priorart/bench.py`):
259	
260	```
261	6 transcripts, 2.26 MB, 456 usage rows, one full pass = 16 ms   [6 minutes in]
262	```
263	
264	16 ms/s is nothing — but the cost is linear in transcript size, which grows for
265	the whole run. Extrapolating from the measured rate (~0.38 MB per agent per
266	6 min), a 2-hour six-agent implement loop reaches ~45 MB, i.e. **~300+ ms of
267	JSON parsing every single second**, on the *same single thread* that tails the
268	journal, classifies spawns, and runs the completion debounce. Touch wants to
269	watch whole sessions, whose transcripts are larger still (this session's
270	`<sessionId>.jsonl` is 777 KB after ~30 minutes).

272	**Recommendation.** Apply the module's own checkpoint pattern one level down:
273	store `{path: (byte_offset, partial_usage_totals)}` per transcript in
274	`.watcher-state.json` and only parse the appended tail — `read_new_lines()`
275	(`:470-491`) is already exactly the right primitive and is already tested.
276	Message-id dedup still works because you keep the accumulated id set (or, since
277	ids are per-message and monotonic, just the running sums plus a small
278	recently-seen id window). Migration consequence: `.watcher-state.json` gains a
279	key; `load_state()`'s journal-identity reset (`:494-512`) already handles a
280	stale/incompatible checkpoint by discarding it.

284	## PRIORART-8 — Full replay from byte 0 on every connect, one WS frame per event, no log trimming — and the UI offers a 500 ms full-resync button
285	
286	**File**: `monitor_server.py:358-378` (`stream_events`, `offset = 0`, one
287	`writer.write(ws_frame(line))` per line), `monitor.html:699-708` (clear + rebuild
288	on every `onopen`), `:390-391` (unbounded `log.insertBefore` + `render()` on
289	every event), `:172-181` and `:714-732` (`rateSel` / `forceResync`)
290	**Severity**: major
291	
292	**Scenario.** There is no resume cursor: every `/ws` connection replays the file
293	from offset 0 as individual text frames, and the page throws away all DOM and
294	accumulators and rebuilds. Then:
295	
296	- `render()` runs on **every** event and re-`appendChild`s **every** card
297	  (`monitor.html:220-238`) — O(events × plans) DOM moves during replay.
298	- log `<li>`s are never trimmed (`:390`), so replay materialises one DOM node
299	  per historical event.
300	- the refresh dropdown offers **500 ms**, and `forceResync()` implements it by
301	  *closing and reopening the socket* (`:717-724`) — i.e. a full history replay
302	  twice per second.
303	
304	Measured on the live run: **375 events / 150 871 bytes in ~6 minutes** for a
305	single six-agent research phase — ~1.5 MB/h, dominated by the quiet 1 Hz token
306	ticks (`decision_watcher.py:781-791`). One hour of history on the 500 ms setting
307	is ≈3 MB/s of replay per open tab, and ≈21 600 log DOM nodes. Touch's terminal
308	view (which must replay a session transcript, already 777 KB at 30 min) makes
309	this the dominant cost of the whole product.
310	
311	**Recommendation.** Add `?from=<byte-offset>` (or `?after=<seq>`) to `/ws`,
312	batch replay into multi-line frames, emit an explicit `{"kind":"replay-end"}`
313	marker, cap the client log with a ring buffer, and coalesce `render()` into a
314	`requestAnimationFrame`. Migration consequence: the client must persist a
315	cursor and keep its accumulators across reconnects — which means giving up the
316	"full replay is safe against double counting" invariant that the current design
317	leans on (`monitoring.md:172-175`); the replacement invariant is
318	"events are ordered and idempotent by seq", which is stronger and is what a
319	control plane needs anyway.

331	task in a task registry — the binary contains
332	`i.type==="local_workflow" && i.status==="running" && i.workflowRunId===e.resumeFromRunId`
333	and the user-facing string *"Workflow ${runId} is still running (task ${id}).
334	Stop it first with TaskStop({taskId: …}) before resuming."* And, decisively:
335	
336	> *"It may have been stopped (via the UI or TaskStop — **these leave no
337	> transcript marker**), or it may have been running when the previous Claude
338	> Code process exited."*
339	
340	So a stopped workflow and a stalled workflow produce **byte-identical**
341	journals. The watcher's only terminal signal is the 60-second quiet debounce
342	(`:738-760`), which will confidently emit

344	open plan card by `state["decisive"]` (`:748-753`) — i.e. it will fabricate a
345	verdict for a run the user *paused on purpose*, and the fabricated verdict will

349	itself (an append-only control log: `paused|resumed|stopped|started`, with

351	control log winning. Concretely: gate the quiet-debounce close behind "no

358	## PRIORART-10 — "Restart" is `resumeFromRunId` cache replay into a NEW journal, and the checkpoint model turns that into duplicated history
359	
360	**File**: `decision_watcher.py:494-512` (`load_state` journal-identity reset),
361	`:72-74` (`JOURNAL`/`WF_NAME` fixed at import)
362	**Proof**: binary text *"To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch
363	with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of
364	agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and
365	everything after it runs live."*
366	**Severity**: major
367	
368	**Scenario.** The harness's restart primitive replays cached `agent()` results
369	into a **new run**, with a new runId and (per `nEp()` in the binary, which
370	symlinks a canonical `workflowRunId` path at the `transcriptDir`) a new
371	transcript dir and journal. `load_state()` sees `state["journal"] != JOURNAL`
372	and — correctly, for its own assumptions — resets `offset=0` and discards all
373	derived state. The watcher then re-emits the *entire* spawn/result/token history
374	of the resumed run into the **same** `events.jsonl`, on top of the original
375	run's events. The dashboard replays both: duplicate agent rows (different agent
376	ids), duplicated token deltas on the card counters (`monitor.html:370-372`
377	accumulates unconditionally), and a card whose badge flips through two runs'
378	worth of transitions.
379	
380	Note the harness *does* hand you the dedup key and the prior art ignores it —
381	every journal `started` line carries a content hash:
382	
383	```
384	{"type":"started","key":"v2:c13a866b3bd1e7129557fc996a218a044553d0115ac84c64a6184c41e4042639","agentId":"a2fc883c96ff7b837"}
385	```
386	
387	(verified: `~/.claude/projects/…/subagents/workflows/wf_829e6f58-b2f/journal.jsonl`).
388	`key` is stable across a cached resume; `agentId` is not. The watcher reads only
389	`type` and `agentId` (`:586-587`).

391	**Recommendation.** Key run state by `(runId, key)` rather than by journal path
392	+ agentId: a `started` whose `key` was already emitted is a cache replay and

394	`.watcher-state.json` gains a `keys` map and `load_state`'s hard reset becomes a
395	merge; this is the single change that makes the README's "restart" control
396	truthful rather than duplicative.

471	## PRIORART-14 — `events.jsonl` is multi-writer and its safety rests on an undocumented "one `write()` per record" invariant
472	
473	**File**: `status.sh:28-45` (`python3 … >> "$STATE_DIR/events.jsonl"`),
474	`decision_watcher.py:150-151` (`open(EVENTS,"a")` + one `f.write(line+"\n")`)
475	**Proof**: `/tmp/claude-1000/priorart/interleave.py` and `interleave2.py`
476	**Severity**: minor (today) / blocker (if Touch reuses the file as a transport)
477	
478	**Scenario.** N concurrent agents' `status.sh` calls plus the watcher all append
479	to the same file with no locking. I tested this directly with 4 concurrent
480	writers × 200 records of ~6 KB each:
481	
482	```
483	one write() per record   -> lines=800  corrupted(mixed-writer)=0
484	record split over 2 write() calls -> lines=800  corrupted(mixed-writer)=206
485	```
486	
487	So the current design is genuinely safe — Linux serialises a single `O_APPEND`
488	`write()` on a regular file — but *only* because every writer today happens to
489	emit a whole record in exactly one syscall (`print()` on a buffered stdout that
490	is flushed once at process exit; a single `f.write()`). Nothing documents this,
491	nothing tests it, and it is exactly the invariant a new writer breaks: a Node.js
492	`stream.write()` of a large payload, an incrementally-built line, or anything
493	streaming terminal output in chunks produces the 206/800 case.
494	
495	**Recommendation.** Write the invariant down next to the schema in
496	`monitoring.md`, and add it to `test_shell.py` as a concurrency test (it is a
497	20-line stdlib test). For Touch: do **not** carry terminal I/O over a shared
498	append-only file — use one file per writer, or a socket. Migration consequence:
499	none for the existing event stream; it decides Touch's terminal transport.

528	
529	**File**: `decision_watcher.py:330-367` (up to `retries=3` × `time.sleep(0.5)`),

509	  the repo already runs under two interpreters. Declare **3.11+** and assert it at
510	  daemon start with a clear message rather than a SyntaxError.
511	
512	---
513	
514	## STACK-17 — Repo layout: app source must not live under `.claude/`
515	**Evidence** — CLAUDE.md:47-49,203-212 declare `.claude/` to be
516	skills + a *stateless* shared module + per-task state. `.gitignore:9` ignores
517	`.claude/local-orchestrators/*/*.log` only; `:18-19` ignore `node_modules/` and
518	`dist/`. `test_shell.py:155-161` asserts the two monitoring ignore lines are
519	present, so `.gitignore` edits must be additive.
520	
521	**Severity: minor**
522	
523	**Recommendation**
524	```
525	aggregator/          # python package: server.py, ws.py, pty.py, sessions.py, model.py
526	touch-visual/        # index.html, app.js, graph.js, terminal.js, style.css
527	touch-visual/vendor/ # xterm.js + xterm.css, pinned + committed (VERSIONS.txt with sha256)
528	tests/               # test_*.py + run_all.sh, stdlib only, executable
529	```
530	Add to `.gitignore`: `aggregator/__pycache__/`, `*.pyc` (already covered by
531	`__pycache__/`), and whatever runtime state Touch writes (e.g.
532	`.touch/` for scrollback spool / pty logs) — while preserving lines 5-6 verbatim
533	so `test_shell.py` keeps passing. Do **not** put Touch state inside
534	`.claude/local-orchestrators/` — that directory is monitoring history that
535	CLAUDE.md forbids deleting.
536	
537	---
538	
539	## STACK-18 — "Pause / restart a loop" has no external API; the control plane is *typed input into an owned PTY*, and that is racy
540	**Evidence**
541	- Binary strings, verbatim:
542	  `Resume the paused workflow by calling: Workflow({scriptPath: '…', resumeFromRunId: '…'})`,
543	  `completed agents return cached results.`,
544	  `To resume after editing the script, call: Workflow({scriptPath: '…', resumeFromRunId: '…'})`.
545	  Resumption is an **in-session tool call**, i.e. it happens because the model in
546	  that session decides to make it.
547	- The journal is the only external artefact and it is append-only observation:
548	  `wf_829e6f58-b2f/journal.jsonl` currently holds six `{"type":"started",…}`
549	  records and nothing else.
550	- The only readiness signal is `status` in `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`
551	  (`idle|busy|…`, plus `waitingFor`), and it is written by the session itself with
552	  **no heartbeat** (STACK-12).
553	- A genuinely local PTY-over-unix-socket surface *does* exist, but only for
554	  background agents: `ps aux` shows
555	  `claude bg-pty-host --bg-pty-host /tmp/cc-daemon-1000/939665dd/pty/8084340e.sock 200 50 -- …`,
556	  and `/tmp/cc-daemon-1000/939665dd/` contains `control.sock`, `pty/<id>.sock`,
557	  `spare/<id>.{pty,claim}.sock`, `rv/<id>.sock`. It is undocumented, has a
558	  hard-coded 200×50 geometry, and its layout is version-coupled to the binary.
559	
560	**Severity: major**
561	
562	**Scenario** — the control buttons are wired to "write text into the PTY". The
563	user clicks *Pause* while the session is mid-tool-call (`status: "busy"`): the
564	text lands in the input queue and is executed minutes later, or is swallowed by a
565	permission dialog (`waitingFor: "dialog open"`), or interleaves with a
566	`--dangerously-skip-permissions` run that is already editing files. The button
567	appears to do nothing, then does something unexpected.
568	
569	**Recommendation**
570	- Implement control as **queued, acknowledged intents**, not fire-and-forget
571	  keystrokes: the button enqueues, the daemon writes only when the session's
572	  `status` is `idle`, and the UI shows `queued → sent → observed` where "observed"
573	  is a *derived* confirmation from `events.jsonl`/journal, not an assumption.
574	- Give each verb an honest definition and label it in the UI:
575	  *Start* = spawn a new owned session and send the skill invocation;
576	  *Restart* = new session + `Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId})` (cached
577	  agents make this cheap, per the binary's own text);
578	  *Terminate* = the STACK-7 ladder;
579	  *Pause* = **stop at the next boundary** (do not send the next prompt / stop
580	  spawning the next attempt), never `SIGSTOP`. Mid-`agent()` there is no
581	  resumable boundary — `implement.workflow.js:168-206` shows the loop's state is
582	  `openFindings` + files on disk, and the skills' invariant is a brand-new
583	  subagent every attempt.
584	- Do not build on `/tmp/cc-daemon-1000/**`. Record it in the design doc as
585	  "exists, deliberately not used", with the reason (undocumented, fixed geometry,
586	  version-coupled, background-only) so the next person does not re-discover it and
587	  assume it was missed.
588	
589	---
590	
591	## Summary of stack decisions this perspective recommends
592	
593	| Concern | Decision | Driven by |
594	|---|---|---|
595	| Runtime | Python 3.11+ asyncio, single process, single port | STACK-6, STACK-15 |
596	| PTY | stdlib `pty.openpty` + `Popen(start_new_session=True)` + `loop.add_reader` | STACK-5, STACK-6 |
597	| Transport | new RFC-6455 codec; `/pty` event-driven, `/ws` 0.5 s file-tail | STACK-4, STACK-5 |
598	| Terminal | vendored xterm.js (489 KB + 7 KB CSS), no bundler | STACK-9 |
599	| Graph | hand-rolled layered SVG, stable node ids, incremental patch | STACK-10 |
600	| Deps | stdlib at runtime, npm only to vendor committed assets, zero page-load fetches | STACK-8 |
601	| Data access | typed projected endpoints over `~/.claude`; no path parameter | STACK-11 |
602	| Sessions | `(pid, procStart)` identity; fast `/proc` liveness + slow `claude agents --json` | STACK-12 |
603	| Auth | token + Origin allowlist; default bind 127.0.0.1 | STACK-3 |
604	| Control | queued intents gated on `status: idle`; documented escalation ladder | STACK-7, STACK-18 |
605	| Layout | `aggregator/`, `touch-visual/`, `tests/` at repo root | STACK-17 |
606

20	- Main page: a terminal-styled web view over a Claude Code session — this is

33	## 2. Facts the driver VERIFIED directly (primary-source, high confidence)

35	### Session registry — `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json`
36	One file per running CLI process. Observed live:
37	```json
38	{"pid":622,"sessionId":"dd469822-…","cwd":"/home/laniakea/Projects/touch",
39	 "startedAt":1784946693282,"procStart":"10028","version":"2.1.220","peerProtocol":1,
40	 "kind":"interactive","entrypoint":"cli","name":"touch-2b","nameSource":"derived",
41	 "status":"busy","updatedAt":…,"statusUpdatedAt":…}

43	- `status` ∈ `idle | busy | waiting | shell`; `waitingFor` gives the reason
44	  (`"input needed"`, `"sandbox request"`, `"dialog open"`, `"worker request"`).
45	- Binary's parser accepts a superset: `messagingSocketPath`, `logPath`, `jobId`,

49	  **no heartbeat** — a killed session leaves `status:"busy"` forever.

51	  stable pid. Key on `pid+procStart`, never on sessionId.

53	### Session transcript — `~/.claude/projects/<cwd-slug>/<sessionId>.jsonl`

63	  isImage, noOutputExpected}`; Read `{type, file}`; Write/Edit include

122	## 3. Two independent feasibility assessments already collected
123	
124	Both returned **feasible-with-caveats** and converged: reading is solved; the
125	terminal and control halves are not.
126	
127	### Assessment A — data layer
128	- Grepped every file under `~/.claude` <20 MB for `\x1b[`: **zero hits**. No
129	  PTY/ANSI bytes, no scrollback, anywhere on disk.
130	- **`thinking` blocks persist EMPTY** (`thinking:""` + signature only) — 32/32

132	  never written to disk.
133	- Write latency measured ≈5 s and **per completed message** — batched via

135	  90 s turn (observed `durationMs: 90511`) is a 90 s void in the files.
136	- Hook surface enumerated from the binary: `PreToolUse, PostToolUse,
137	  PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, Notification, UserPromptSubmit,
138	  UserPromptExpansion, SessionStart, SessionEnd, Stop, StopFailure,
139	  SubagentStart, SubagentStop, PreCompact, PostCompact, PermissionRequest,

154	### Assessment B — control layer
155	- `/proc/<pid>/fd` for the live session: only `/dev/pts/0` + outbound sockets.
156	  `ss -lnpx` and `ss -lntp` return **nothing** — no unix or TCP listener exists.
157	  `dev.tty.legacy_tiocsti = 0`, so TTY keystroke injection is off. An

174	- Other input paths, all constrained: `--bg-pty-host` attach (daemon workers

188	## 4. Explicitly UNVERIFIED (do not treat as settled)
